headline: A second KOSPI crash (−6%, circuit breaker) and a 6bp overnight Treasury rally push KTBs lower again: the 3Y leads, −5.6bp to 3.613%, the 10Y falls 3.4bp to 3.853% and 3s10s re-steepens to 24bp
summary: KTBs rallied for a fourth day, but this time the front end led: the 2Y fell 5.4bp to 3.601% and the 3Y 5.6bp to 3.613% (61bp over the base rate), against −3.4bp for the 10Y (3.853%) and −2.7bp for the 30Y (3.971%), so 3s10s steepened 2.2bp to 24.0bp after Thursday's 1-year low of 21.8bp. On the week the 3Y is −10.2bp and the 10Y −15.5bp, still a bull flattener. The money market did not move: MSB 91-day 3.174%, CD 3.34% and CP 3.83% left CP–CD at 49bp (97th percentile). Spread products lagged again: AA- 3Y is 70bp over KTB (94th percentile), KEPCO 3Y a new 1-year wide at 46bp and AAA bank 1Y 43bp (94th), while the KDB 3Y fit tightened 1.9bp to 23bp.
drivers: Fears of US curbs on AI data centres hit chips again: KOSPI fell 324 points (−6.02%) to 5,059.69 after an intraday −8.8% triggered a circuit breaker, taking the two-day loss to 11% and the index about 44% below its June peak. Foreigners sold about KRW 2.8tn of KOSPI stock (more than KRW 30tn over a month), VKOSPI closed at 65 and the won fell 14.5 to 1,356.6 per dollar, its biggest drop since May. Safe-haven buying kept bonds bid all day, though the weaker won capped the long end.
US Treasuries explain most of today's move

In New York on Thursday the US 10Y par yield fell 6bp to 4.84% and the 2Y about 11bp as the Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, even though jobless claims fell to 189k (196k expected) and productivity beat; December Fed hike odds slipped to about 70% from 83%. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 that implies −2.8bp for the KTB 10Y against an actual −3.4bp, so about four-fifths of today was global, unlike Thursday's mostly local rally. The KTB–UST 10Y gap is −99bp, still the widest of the past year.
Futures: foreigners switch back to the 3Y

Foreigners bought 7,422 3Y KTB futures and sold 521 10Y, reversing Thursday's 10Y buying; the 3Y rose 16 ticks to 103.85 and the 10Y 18 ticks to 109.37. Against our basket fair values (3Y 103.96, 10Y 109.44) the 3Y settled 11 ticks cheap (about 3.8bp) and the 10Y 7 ticks cheap (under 1bp), so the front end still has room to catch up.

Citi still expects a November 26 hike despite the equity crash and sees 3.50% by February, and the market agrees: MSB 91-day, CD and CP were unchanged, although CP's 30-session climb finally paused. With the 3Y now only 61bp over the 3.00% base rate, dealers see little room below 3.55–3.60% until hike pricing fades. Governor Lee is at the BIS meetings in Basel through Nov 11.
data: Record, first month above USD 60bn; supports the won and the BOK's hawkish lean, little KTB impact.
In line to a touch soft; the fuel price cap flatters headline, so it does not rule out a November 26 hike.
Strong end-user demand; the 30Y now trades about 7bp below the auction yield.
Trade strength underpins the won and the BOK's hawkish lean.
Fastest output gain since 2011; keeps hike pricing in the 1–2Y.
Large beat on chip capex and government spending; private consumption fell 0.2%.
Hold at 3.00%, unanimous (after +25bp in July and August)
Guided to staying restrictive; a November 26 hike to 3.25% remains the front-end base case.
view: This week's rally is now split about evenly: over four weeks the 10Y is −54bp, of which −28bp is US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.63 and −27bp is Korea's own equity-to-bond rotation, and today was mostly the global part (about 2.8bp of 3.4bp). The rotation signal rose to +2.04 (bond rally) as KOSPI fell 24% in four weeks and margin credit 15%, and it has been right since Oct 8, but the curve has priced much of it: 1s2s is 5bp (1-year low) and the 3Y sits only 11bp above a 3.50% terminal. With US payrolls tonight, 3Y/10Y/30Y Treasury auctions next week and a November 26 hike still priced, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.78–3.95% over the next two weeks; I would not chase below 3.85% and would buy a back-up toward 3.95–4.00%. I stay flat the curve after Thursday's stop (3s10s has since bounced to 24bp) until KOSPI stabilises. The signal still works better against Treasuries (hedged rally calls right 66% of the time and sell-off calls 69%, against 48% and 57% outright; Sharpe 1.31 vs 1.00), so a KTB 10Y long against about 0.6 × US 10Y remains the cleaner trade than outright duration at the widest KTB–UST gap of the year.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 5.4bp to 3.601%, 57th percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.37%), while the 1Y fell only 1.6bp to 3.551% (85th), so 1s2s is 5.0bp, a 1-year low (average 30bp). MSB 91-day 3.174% is at the 96th percentile: the bill curve still prices a November 26 hike, and the 2Y is now pricing some of the cycle's end.
buckets.call: No trigger hit (2Y 3.601% vs the 3.60% fade level). Keep: fade a close below 3.60% (target 3.70%, stop 3.52%); add above 3.80%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s steepened 2.2bp to 24.0bp, 1st percentile of its 1-year range (average 40bp), the day after our steepener from 29bp was stopped at 21.8bp (−7.2bp). Foreigners bought 3Y and sold 10Y futures today, but one day's bounce against a 5.3bp weekly flattening is not a turn.
buckets.call: Stay flat. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures) only once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; then target 30bp, stop 18bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.853% is at the 46th percentile of a 3.20–4.60% range (average 3.90%), −15.5bp this week and −54bp over four weeks. The old 3.98–4.02% buy zone was not reached; the KTB–UST gap of −99bp is a 1-year extreme, so an outright long has little cushion if Treasuries sell off.
buckets.call: Buy zone moved to 3.95–4.00% (was 3.98–4.02%, not reached) as the range shifted lower; stop 4.10%, target 3.80%. Don't chase below 3.85%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s widened 0.6bp to +2.9bp, the 98th percentile (average −9.5bp), as the 30Y (−2.7bp) outpaced the 50Y (−2.1bp); the switch from +2.5bp is 0.4bp against us. The long end lagged the belly again (10s20s30s fly +2.9bp to 11.4bp). On Thursday's trades the 2050 bond (21-2, 32 trades) was about 7bp cheap to the curve, while 3Y-futures bond 25-10 (118 trades) was 2.5bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 0.4bp against.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (22 trades) puts the 3Y 22.9bp over KTB, down 1.9bp and now the 69th percentile (average 19bp), so the overweight from about 26bp is 3.2bp in favour. The 1Y fit is 35bp over (96th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 32bp (86th, average 24bp). KEXIM shows 20bp on only 3 trades (low confidence), and the 5Y fits are flat extrapolations, so ignore them.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, 3.2bp in favour.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (51-trade fit) is 42.6bp over the 1Y KTB, the 94th percentile (average 31bp), and 37bp at 2Y (89th). CD 3.34% and CP 3.83% are both 1-year highs and CP–CD is 49bp (97th percentile, average 28bp); CP's run of rises paused today. IBK 1Y (18 trades) is 35bp over, 87th percentile.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 4.5bp to 4.313%, 1.1bp less than the KTB, so the spread is 70bp (94th percentile, average 61bp); KEPCO 3Y at 46bp over is a new 1-year wide and BBB- minus AA- is 583bp (75th). Credit is cheapening slowly through two equity crashes, without forced selling.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US October payrolls (Fri Nov 6, 22:30 KST), US 3Y/10Y/30Y auctions (Nov 9, 10, 12), Korea November 1–10 exports around Nov 11, BOK Governor at the BIS in Basel to Nov 11, then the BOK meeting on Nov 26; a KOSPI rebound with foreigners turning buyers, or a Treasury sell-off on payrolls or weak auctions, is the main risk to the rally.
